newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Mobutu lives in Swiss luxury amid Zaire crisis.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu lives in Swiss luxury amid Zaire crisis.

text.p: Scarcely can a man's absence and silence have been more noticeable: east Zaire is in crisis, the U.N. has lost contact with 500,000 refugees on the run and aid agencies are scrambling to find a way out.

But away from all these troubles, Zaire's stricken leader Mobutu Sese Seko is living in luxury in one of the world's most exclusive hotels on the shores of Lake Geneva in the Swiss town of Lausanne where he is undergoing cancer treatment.

The 66-year-old Zairean president, in Switzerland since August, and his entourage of more than 20 bodyguards and aides, have occupied part of the fourth-floor suites at the glamorous neo-Baroque Beau-Rivage Palace hotel in Lausanne.
"He's here. He's upstairs. He rarely comes out of his room," a hotel employee whispered on Wednesday when pressed by visiting journalists about Mobutu's movements.

Mobutu has yet to comment publicly on the reports of looting, fighting, refugees on the run and towns changing hands in the east of his vast, anarchic Central Afican country -- which diplomats say is under serious threat of disintegration.

Swiss secrecy and discreet security surround him. His rare sightings include brief visits to the University Hospital where he underwent prostate cancer surgery on August 22 and those at gourmet restaurants in town.
When Mobutu, who stands six feet (1.8 metres) tall, ventures out, he is noticeable by his trademark leopardskin fur hat, witnesses say.

Mobutu has installed his own Zairean telephone operator at the hotel. His prime minister Kengo wa Dondo was here for a visit only last week. U.N. Secretary General Boutros Boutros-Ghali has telephoned him in the past few days.

Hotel officials say Mobutu has been having some surprising visitors lately. They said former French interior minister Charles Pasqua paid an informal visit to the president on Tuesday. "He just showed up," said one. "And there are plenty of others."
Pasqua's office confirmed he was in Switzerland on Tuesday but gave no details.
Mobutu, a pariah banned from much of Western Europe and the United States, has more than $4 billion stashed away in Swiss bank accounts, according to Swiss media reports.
Swiss media estimate the hotel bill for Mobutu and his entourage at close to two million Swiss francs ($1.6 million) and say they have been made to pay in advance.
Mobutu's personal suite at the hotel, at times occupied by monarchs including Spain's King Juan Carlos and Jordan's King Hussein, was priced at 2,400 swiss francs ($2,000) a night.
"He's our client, just like any other client," hotel manager Christian Marich told Reuters. "Mobutu has a lot of visitors. We respect his privacy."

Marich said there were no special food deliveries for Mobutu. The president often dined on fish and fried potatoes, he said. "There's no champagne, no caviar, nothing special -- just grilled fish and fried potatoes," he said.
Meanwhile, discontent is growing over Mobutu's presence among Swiss residents and politicians who say they want the dictator out.
Parliamentarian Joseph Zisyadis told Reuters that local deputies were ready to vote for a motion asking the Swiss federal government to push Mobutu out of Lausanne.
"It's a scandal. This dictator starves his people, his country is in war and this dictator speaks about his country's situation from our own country," said an angry Zisyadis.
